texts.facts: The marriage of the parties is replete with gross emotional verbal and economic abuse and neglect and when their relationship got strained, respondent no.1 /complainant filed a petition under Section 12 of the DV Act before the learned trial court alleging therein various incidents of immense cruelty, emotional abuse, physical and mental abuse, economic abuse and psychological abuse inflicted upon her by the appellant. She has alleged that appellant has willfully neglected, abused and demeaned the respondents and son Aadidev and also refused to maintain and provide them adequately as per the lifestyle and status.
texts.arguments: Whereas, the respondent no.1 and children have a right to live with dignity in the shared household Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr. Page No.9 of 16 which includes a right to privacy and peace and a right to food. It has also been stated that the appellant has not come to the court with clean hands and has misrepresented to this court and the present appeal is nothing but an abuse of the process of law. The appellant has not been ousted from the shared household nor has he been rendered roofless.

8. Before proceeding to deal with the matter, it shall be apposite to Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia &
Anr. Page No.11 of 16 notice the scope of an appeal under Section 29 of the DV Act.

Jurisdiction of appellate court under section 29 of DV Act with respect to an order passed under Section 23 of the DV Act is limited to ascertaining if the Trial Court has committed any irregularity or perversity in reaching the finding.

This view regarding scope of appeal u/sec.-29 PW DV Act with respect to orders passed u/sec.-23 of PW DV Act was taken by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in Abhijeet Bhikaseth Auti Vs. State of Maharashtra & Anr. reported as 2009 Crl. Law Jou

Relevant portion of the judgment is reproduced herein below:-
"24...........

Thus, the conclusion, which can be summarized are as under:
(i)........
(ii)........
(iii) An appeal will also lie against orders passed under sub- section (1) and sub-section (2) of the Section 23 of the said Act which are passed by the le

However, while dealing with an appeal against the order passed under Section 23 of the said Act, the Appellate Court will usually not interfere with the exercise of discretion by the learned Magistrate.

The appellate Court will interfere only if it is found that the discretion has been exercised arbitrarily, capriciously, perversely or if it is found that the Court has ignored settled Amritesh Jatia vs Vidhi Jatia on 12 July, 2024 Indian K

It is pertinent to mention here that at the time of filing of the appeal, the matter was remanded back to the learned MM for fresh hearing on the point of relief concerning restraining the appellants to refuse food to respondents no.1 and c
Perusal of the trial court record indicates that the matter is still pending adjudication in this regard.

Besides granting ex-parte relief, the appellant has also been directed to remove all his belongings from 2nd floor of the property.

12. Perusal of the impugned order indicates that learned MM while passing the impugned order has simply relied upon the application filed by respondent no.1 and observed that she suffered domestic violence at the hands of respondents.

The relevant extract of the impugned order is reproduced as under :
"Perusal of the application along with supporting affidavit prima facie shows that complainant was in a domestic relationship with respondents and she suffered domestic vio

The complainant has also placed reliance on order dated 04.11.2023 of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, according to which MCD was directed to de-seal the second floor of the property by 05.11.2023...."

13. From the above, it is evident that learned MM has only considered the allegations made in the application and the documents relied upon by respondent no.1 and passed the impugned order restraining the appellant and his parents from forc
14. The Domestic Violence Act emphasizes the need for a fair hearing.
Ex-parte relief may be granted in urgent situations, but the principle of natural justice requires that all parties have an opportunity to present their case.
The Act does not support granting relief without hearing the respondent unless there is a compelling reason to do so.

The court acknowledges the complainant's / respondent's concern regarding her safety and her right to reside in the shared household but at the same time, it cannot be ignored that the appellant has a right to be heard and to defend against

In the present case, the respondent no.1's apprehension is that appellant in connivance with MCD officials is trying to dispossess her and the children from the shared household.
It may be Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr.
Page No.14 of 16 mentioned that the appellant himself is a victim of the sealing of the property.
Admittedly, his belongings and clothes are lying on 2nd floor.
It does not appeal to the reason that why will he intentionally got sealed his valuable items.
Thus, the issuance of an ex-parte order directing him to remove his belongings from 2 nd floor of the property without hearing him violates the principles of natural justice.
Further, at the time of granting ex-parte relief, the court is required to assess whether the respondent/complainant demonstrated a genuine sense of urgency warranting ex-parte relief.
The absence of imminent danger or a credible threat to the respondent's safety raises concerns about the necessity of immediate judicial intervention.
The order passed by learned MM appears to reflect a mechanical manner rather than a reasoned approach.
16. Perusal of the impugned order further shows that learned MM has also failed to consider the ongoing mediation going on between the parties.
Learned MM's failure to consider this context suggests that an oversight in evaluating the overall circumstances surrounding the case.
17. In view of the above findings, the case is remanded back to the learned MM for a thorough re-evaluation of the facts and circumstances of the case.

Learned MM is also directed to hear both parties afresh giving them equal opportunity to present their Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr.
Page No.15 of 16 case.
With these observations, the appeal stands disposed of.
The impugned order dated 16.12.2023 is set aside.
